title: Safeguard upgrades & tenant isolation for Dedicated control planes (multi-region failover & load-shedding)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: As more customers adopt Dedicated and Private deployments, we need stronger isolation guarantees and safer upgrade/failover procedures to prevent tenant blast radius during incidents. Scope: 1) Define SLO impact accounting for Dedicated tenants during partial region failures. 2) Implement isolated control plane primitives (per-tenant change windows, safe-config gating). 3) Add circuit breakers and graduated load-shedding at the tenant boundary to protect GPU pools. 4) Safe rollout primitives + automatic rollback triggers for control-plane upgrades. Deliverables: - SLO doc & incident accounting template for Dedicated tenants. - Runtime circuit breaker library + operator config (tenant-level thresholds). - Load-shedding policy engine with prioritization: critical routes > best-effort routes. - Upgrade safety runbook + canary gating in the private control plane. Considerations and trade-offs: - Preferring tenant-level isolation increases orchestration complexity (more control plane objects) but reduces cross-tenant impact. - Aggressive load-shedding reduces availability for noisy tenants; we need transparent customer communication and per-tenant override options for enterprise customers. - Circuit breakers must be fast and local (node/edge) to avoid control-plane amplification; but local decisions can be less globally optimal. Planned migration: start with a single Dedicated region (us-west-2) for experiments, then extend to multi-region orchestration with failover routing rules. Compatibility: must work with existing KV cache and batching layers; avoid adding per-request latency > 3ms on median. Security review: required for tenant isolation APIs and audit logs.
